title: Build ramp rocks under a rover's wheels to roll it up a ledge
instruction: The rover can't climb the ledge on its own. Get it up onto the ledge without lifting it.
context: Off-road recovery crews get a vehicle up a ledge its wheels cannot climb by stacking rocks into a ramp under each wheel, then winching or driving it up; a free wheel jams against any step taller than its radius. Here the robot must set two stepped rocks at the vehicle's track spacing, high step against the ledge, and push the rover up them, without lifting or tipping it. Unlike TK-W67CJE (one ramp set against a step's face for a wheelchair), TK-UYFM6W (two flat runners laid into fixed seats across a level gap) and TK-NBL9FR (the attendant's tip-back technique for a wheelchair at a kerb, which this task forbids), there are no seats or marks: each ramp's place is read from the rover's own wheel lines, and the wheels must be raised by built supports over a step 1.4 times their radius, and the failure is a wheel jamming at the step.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Lower track: an earth-brown sheet 0.6 mm thick (painted PVC foil), taped down on the table from x 6 to 44, y -17 to 17. Ledge: a fixed deck of plywood, clamped to the table, 3.8 cm tall, from x 44 (its face, toward the robot) to 74, y -17 to 17, its top painted earth brown and its sides rock grey. Rover: a 1:18 trail crawler (Traxxas TRX-4M with the Bronco body shell, decals removed, painted yellow with a white roof), 26.2 x 12.4 x 11.7 cm, 0.51 kg, tyres 5.6 cm across, motor pinion removed so its wheels roll freely, on the lower track facing the ledge, the midpoint between its axles at (24.5, 0), its front tyres 9 cm short of the ledge. Ramp rocks (four, grey, 3D-printed PLA hollow-filled with steel shot to 150 g each): each a three-step block 6 cm long and 4 cm wide with steps 2 cm long and 1.27, 2.53 and 3.8 cm tall; lying on the table beside the track at (20, 23) and (20, -23) with their high ends away from the robot, and at (31, 24) and (31, -24) turned 23 and 160 degrees anticlockwise (seen from above) from high-end-away-from-the-robot.
scoring: 0 if at any time any tyre is more than 1 cm above the surface under it for 0.5 s, or more than 1.8 cm above it even for one control step (the rover lifted, hopped, or tipped up by one end; surfaces are the track, the ledge top and the steps of ramp rocks lying flat on the table; a tyre on a ramp step never rises more than one step, 1.27 cm, while a bare tyre must rise 2.8 cm to cross the face); a front tyre reaches the ledge without a ramp rock set under its own line at that moment (as in the 0.25 clause); or the rover tilts more than 30 degrees. Otherwise, at the end, with the rover and the ramp rocks at rest (each moving under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s for the last 20 control steps, 1 s at 20 Hz) and released (none of six points on each arm, its wrist joint, palm, both fingertips, tool point and the point between the pad tips, and no point along the arm from its shoulder joint to its palm, within 5 cm of the rover or a ramp rock): 1.0 if all four tyres rest on the ledge (each tyre's lowest point within 1 cm of the ledge top and inside its outline) with the rover within 10 degrees of level; 0.5 if both front tyres rest on the ledge; 0.25 if under each front wheel's line (the y of that front tyre's centre, the rover facing the ledge within 15 degrees), a ramp rock lies flat on the table (tilted under 10 degrees) with its high step facing the ledge (within 20 degrees), the end of that step from 5 mm short of the ledge's face to 6 mm past it (pressed on the face), and its centre within 1.5 cm of the wheel's line; otherwise 0. A full score ends the trial once it has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Roll the rover back to its mark; lay the four ramp rocks back at their marks beside the track.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The rover base is one rigid body at the crawler's published size and mass; wheels roll freely with 0.002 N m s/rad drag (pinion removed); suspension rigid. Tyre diameter 5.6 cm is estimated; the 3.8 cm ledge jams a bare wheel even if the real tyre is a little larger. Friction: tyres 1.0, rocks 1.0, ledge 0.8. Ramp rocks are stepped blocks. Lifting is judged from tyre heights. No forces or damage are simulated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms moved over the rocks beside the rover without setting one at the ledge; the rover stayed at the foot of the ledge); demo: 1.0
